parts.label: (a)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
$4\cos^4x+\cos^2x-3=0$, factorising to $(4\cos^2x-3)(\cos^2x+1)=0$ — M1; attempt to solve the three-term quartic or quadratic in another variable.
$\cos^2x=\frac34$ (and $\cos^2x=-1$) — A1. If M0, SC B1 for sight of both values.
$\cos x=\pm\sqrt{\text{their }\frac34}=\pm\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$ — M1. Square-root their $\cos^2x$; allow without $\pm$, implied by correct answers; ignore $\sqrt{-1}$.
$x=\frac\pi6,\frac{5\pi}6,\frac{7\pi}6,\frac{11\pi}6$ — A1 A1 FT. One A1 for any two correct exact answers and one for all four with no others in range; FT for appropriate reflected exact answers. SC B1 for all four in degrees or non-exact only. Total: 5.

parts.label: (b)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
$\cos^2x=\frac{-1-\sqrt{1+16k}}8<0$, hence no solutions — B1. State this root is less than zero and link to $\cos^2x$; may substitute a value $k\ge0$.
$\cos^2x=\frac{-1\pm\sqrt{1+16k}}8$ — *M1. Must use quadratic formula; allow any $k$ except $\pm3$; condone $+$ rather than $\pm$.
Substitute $k=5$ and obtain $1$ from the positive-root formula, or argue $k>5\Rightarrow1+16k>81$ — DM1.
$\cos^2x\ge1$ (with equality at $5$ and greater when $k>5$) — A1; link to $\cos^2x$.
Conclude after considering both signs that there are no solutions — A1; dependent on all previous marks. Alternative inequality route with the same root formula and allocations accepted. Total: 5.
